html:
The Otomí, who call themselves Hñähñu, are one of the oldest peoples of central Mexico, living in the highlands of today's Hidalgo, Querétaro, the State of Mexico and nearby. Their languages belong to the Oto-Manguean family, one of the oldest in Mesoamerica.

Otomí people probably made up part of the population of Tula and other early cities. In the 1300s they had their own city-state at Xaltocan, which fell to its neighbours in the late 1300s. Under the Aztec Triple Alliance many Otomí paid tribute, and the Aztecs named a rank of fierce warriors, the otontin, after them. Others lived under the Tlaxcala republic, and Otomí soldiers there fought Hernán Cortés in 1519 before joining him against the Aztecs.

In colonial times Otomí soldiers helped the Spanish settle the dry north, where they founded Querétaro. Many Otomí still live in the Mezquital Valley, growing maize and making goods from agave, and several hundred thousand speak Otomí. See also the map's Otomies and their Nahua neighbours.
